items.question: What is the basic unit of life?
items.explanation: All living things are made of cells. Some, like bacteria, are just one cell. Your body is made of trillions of cells working together.

items.question: Plant cells have a cell wall, but animal cells do not.
items.explanation: The cell wall is a strong outer layer that gives plant cells their fixed shape. Animal cells only have a soft cell membrane. That is why plants can stand tall without bones.

items.question: Which part of the cell is called its "powerhouse" because it releases energy?
items.explanation: Mitochondria break down food to release energy the cell can use. Cells that work hard, like muscle cells, have many mitochondria.

items.question: The part of the cell that controls all its activities is the ___.
items.explanation: The nucleus is like the control room of the cell. It contains the instructions (DNA) for how the cell grows and works.

items.question: Who first saw and named cells, using a simple microscope in 1665?
items.explanation: Robert Hooke looked at a thin slice of cork and saw tiny box-like spaces. They reminded him of small rooms, so he called them "cells".
